import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

path = '/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/32102e3e-d12a-4209-9163-7b3a104efe5d.xlsx'

df['Format'] = np.where(mask_header, df['Title'].astype(str).str.strip(), np.nan)
df['Format'] = df['Format'].ffill()
# Drop the header rows from data usage
content_df = df[~mask_header].copy()
print('Formats present:', content_df['Format'].dropna().unique())
print('Sample Blu-Ray rows:')
print(content_df[content_df['Format']=='Blu-Ray'].head(6))

Given this is a Seattle rental store, the business-relevant interpretation is the oldest Blu-Ray currently rentable (i.e., exclude Missing/Rented/Overdue). I'll filter to Status == 'Available' within Blu-Ray and return the earliest.
```python
# filename: oldest_available_bluray.py
import pandas as pd

path = '/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/32102e3e-d12a-4209-9163-7b3a104efe5d.xlsx'
df = pd.read_excel(path, skiprows=2)
format_set = {'DVD','Blu-Ray','VHS','CD','Digital'}
mask_header = df['Title'].astype(str).str.strip().isin(format_set)
df['Format'] = df['Title'].where(mask_header).ffill()
content_df = df[~mask_header].copy()
bluray = content_df[content_df['Format']=='Blu-Ray'].copy()
bluray['Year'] = pd.to_numeric(bluray['Year'], errors='coerce')
avail = bluray[bluray['Status'].astype(str).str.strip().eq('Available')].dropna(subset=['Year'])
oldest_year = avail['Year'].min()
oldest_title = avail.loc[avail['Year'].eq(oldest_year), 'Title'].iloc[0] if not avail.empty else None
print('Oldest available Blu-Ray:', oldest_title)
```
